Before we start — this is not Dallas
In 1875 a lawyer in Dallas wrote to his local paper that Fort Worth had gone so quiet he had seen a panther asleep in the street.

It was meant as an insult. The editor of the Fort Worth Democrat answered by having a new masthead engraved — a panther, lying down, under a motto:

Where the Panther Laid DownFort Worth Democrat · 1876

The city never gave it back. The panther crouches on Fort Worth police badges to this day, rides on the fire trucks, is carved into the Flatiron Building downtown, and turns up as a school mascot and a lacrosse team. So — Fort Worth, not Dallas. They have had a hundred and fifty years of being told otherwise. WFAA · NBC 5

The Basis

How every number here was arrived at

Nine properties priced, one room and two adults throughout so the totals compare directly. Every figure is the all-in total including taxes and fees, on a rate that can still be cancelled. Every distance is a Google Maps lookup from the property’s own coordinates, not an estimate.

Both stay lengths are priced on every hotel. Each one leads with its two-night total for Saturday to Monday, with the three-night Friday-to-Monday figure directly underneath — so whichever arrival a couple settles on, the comparison holds without anything needing to be repriced. Four couples, so four rooms.

Three things to know before comparing

  • Nobody is renting a car. Everything is rideshare, which changes how the times below should be read. A twenty-minute drive is a twenty-minute fare each way, and Sunday afternoon into Arlington will surge. Anywhere the group can reach on foot is worth more than the price difference suggests — and one hotel can walk to the stadium.
  • Every total was checked against booking the hotel directly. Eight of the nine match the hotel’s own website, several to the exact cent. Nobody needs to go and price-check this themselves.
  • Two properties will not sell a Saturday–Monday stay at all. The Crescent and Hyatt Place Arlington both return a minimum-night requirement for those dates. Both are placed last in their sections for that reason.

The Crescent Hotel, Fort Worth

3300 Camp Bowie Blvd · Cultural District
Three-night minimum this weekendClosest to the museums

A genuine problem rather than a pricing note: The Crescent will not sell a Saturday-to-Monday stay on these dates. Its own booking system rejects the combination outright and suggests extending the stay instead. Anyone arriving Saturday would have to book three nights and pay for a Friday they are not there for — roughly $570 to $620 plus tax per room, for an empty room.

For the two travelling Friday to Monday it works normally, and it is a strong Cultural District option: the museums are a few minutes away and it is eight minutes from the TCU stadium. But it cannot house most of the group without that dead night, which is a different proposition from the rest of this list regardless of what it costs.

Note that the Premier King is both a better room than the Deluxe King and $167 cheaper — they sit on different rate lines.

Live! by Loews — Arlington

1600 E Randol Mill Rd, Arlington · Entertainment District
Walk to the stadiumClosest to the stadium

The only hotel on this list you can walk to the game from, and with no cars in the group that matters more than it would otherwise. 0.7 miles, about 14 minutes on foot. On Sunday the walk will almost certainly beat a ride: no surge pricing, no drop-off queue, and crucially no waiting forty minutes in a stadium lot afterwards with eighty thousand other people trying to leave. Restaurants and the Texas Live! complex are next door, so Sunday evening needs no transport at all.

What it costs is severe. It is the second most expensive on this list for two nights, and the reason is that Arlington prices invert: Sunday is the peak night here, at around $1,679 against $1,487 for Saturday. Where the Fort Worth hotels get cheap on game day, this one gets expensive. It also takes the full amount at booking and its cancellation deadline is the earliest of the nine. Against that, set two days of Arlington fares you would not be paying.

Hotel Vin, Grapevine

215 E Dallas Rd, Grapevine · Main Street district
Closest to the airportFlattest pricingLimited availability

Worth a proper look rather than a glance. It is the airport answer — five minutes to DFW against roughly thirty from Fort Worth — and the assumption would be that it pays for that by being miles from the stadium. It does not. It is 24 minutes to Arlington against 17 to 18 from downtown Fort Worth. It gives up around seven minutes on Sunday and saves around twenty-five on Monday morning, which with no cars is a real difference in both fare and stress on a flight day.

It also sits outside both games, so its pricing barely moves across the weekend — the flattest of the nine. It is a genuine boutique hotel on Grapevine’s Main Street rather than an airport chain, with restaurants and bars walkable from the door, and it is the one option that pairs naturally with the Gaylord Texan attraction opening that Friday. The cost is that it is not in Fort Worth, so the Stockyards and the museums become a deliberate outing.

Standard rates carry no added benefits. The hotel does sell packages — one adds a bottle of wine on arrival, chocolates, Riedel glasses, a spa gift and turndown for around $228 more across the two nights.

Section Three

Dining — and the research behind it

Two dinners to plan for four couples, which changes what is bookable. Here is what was consulted before the list below was arrived at.

This list consolidates Eater, the Michelin Guide, Anthony Bourdain’s Texas coverage, Texas Monthly’s Top 50 barbecue list, local press including Fort Worth Magazine, and Google review volume — not a single source. Every restaurant below has had its address, current opening hours and rating confirmed directly, and every one has had availability for eight checked. Anything that could not be confirmed has been left out rather than guessed at.

Three findings worth stating plainly, because all three were checked rather than skipped:

Michelin2025 and 2026 guides

Fort Worth has no Michelin-starred restaurants. The city was passed over in both guides. One Fort Worth restaurant holds a Bib Gourmand and one Arlington restaurant is Recommended; both are below. The nearest stars are in Dallas, about 40 minutes east.

Chef’s TableNetflix, all seasons

No Dallas–Fort Worth restaurant has ever appeared on the show. The Texas episode features Tootsie Tomanetz at Snow’s BBQ in Lexington — roughly three hours away and open Saturdays only, which is the day of the TCU game. Not workable on this trip.

World’s 50 Best BarsNorth America 2026, positions 1–100

No Dallas–Fort Worth bar appears anywhere on the list. The 2026 rankings were announced in Vancouver in April; Houston is the only Texas city represented across both the top 50 and the extended 51–100. Worth knowing so nobody goes looking. The list

French · 4.6 (572) · Near TCU

From chefs Felipe Armenta and Graham Elliot, and named among Texas Monthly’s best new restaurants. The closest Fort Worth gets to a proper occasion dinner and the strongest option for a group evening. On S. Hulen Street west of the TCU campus, so it pairs naturally with Saturday.

Availability for 8: checked. Bookings run through Tock and the calendar does not yet reach November. Not full — not yet open. Will re-check when the window opens and call if needed.

The headline on availability

  • Not one of these is full. Every obstacle is either a booking calendar that has not opened yet, or a party size that needs a phone call. Nothing is lost by deciding later.
  • With no cars, Don Artemio and il Modo are the two that work without transport — Don Artemio from the Cultural District, il Modo from downtown. Le Margot and Goldee’s are both rides.
  • Smoke’N Ash and Mariano’s are Arlington, so both are Sunday options built around the game rather than evening ones.
  • The Stockyards has around a dozen more bars and restaurants clustered in the restored 1912 barns, all walkable from Hotel Drover. Individual venues are not listed because opening hours for that weekend could not be confirmed.
Before game day
The Statue of Liberty could stand on the star at midfield of AT&T Stadium and, with the roof closed, her torch still wouldn’t touch the ceiling.

Two steel arches, each around 300 feet tall, carry the world’s longest single-span operable roof — about twelve minutes to open or close. The glass doors at each end zone stand 120 feet high and 180 feet wide, the largest operable glass doors anywhere. It cost roughly $1.15 billion and opened in 2009. Sunday’s game is in there. Arlington visitor guide

Section Four

Ideas for Saturday and Sunday

Not a schedule — nothing is fixed and the TCU kickoff time is not announced yet. These are the confirmed options across the weekend, in Fort Worth and the wider Metroplex, with nobody needing a car.

Game day — Sunday at AT&T Stadium

The Miller Lite HouseFree with a game ticket

The strongest find here and it costs nothing extra. Opens four hours before kickoff, so around 11:25am for a 3:25 start, inside the ticketed perimeter. 87,000 square feet with a 70-yard turf field for tailgate games, 50+ TVs, two beer gardens, live music and $5 beers. Effectively a pre-built tailgate, and the right answer for a group without a car — you walk in with your ticket. The first 120 arrivals get a wristband for reserved standing room on the Miller Lite Landing.

Bought-in tailgatesNeeds a phone call

Two operators run turnkey tailgates at or beside the stadium — one on Collins Street directly opposite, about three hours pre-kick with a Texas BBQ buffet and Cowboys alumni; another on official lots with setup and clean-up included. Both normally sell these inside ticket-and-hotel packages. Whether either will sell a tailgate on its own needs a call, and has not been assumed.

Both are drop-off accessible, which the do-it-yourself version is not — stadium tailgating requires your own parked vehicle, so it is off the table for this group.

Getting there and backWorth deciding in advance

Rideshare into the stadium on a game day is straightforward; leaving is the hard part, with surge pricing and long pickup queues once eighty thousand people move at once. Two ways round it: stay in Arlington and walk, or plan to stay somewhere near the stadium for an hour after the whistle and let it clear. The Texas Live! complex next to the stadium exists more or less for that purpose.

Saturday — the TCU game, if the group goes

TCU vs Kansas StateAmon G. Carter Stadium · kickoff TBA

Designated a “Freedom Frogs” military appreciation game. Resale tickets have been running from around $61. The kickoff time is announced roughly two weeks out, which is the single thing most likely to reshape Saturday — an early kick leaves the evening open, a late one takes it. TCU schedule

Frog AlleyFree · opens 3 hrs before kickoff

On the east side of the stadium — food trucks, live music and the team’s Frog Walk entrance. The no-cost version of a tailgate, and walk-in from a drop-off.

Turnkey tailgate at TCUCleaner than the NFL equivalent

TCU’s official fan experience partner runs genuinely turnkey tailgates — setup, breakdown, food and beverage — with custom arrangements for groups. Sites include Schollmaier Lawn in the middle of Frog Alley, the tennis courts, and the alumni centre. Pricing needs a quote, and timing cannot be fixed until the kickoff is announced.

What else is on that weekend

Stockyards Championship RodeoFri & Sat 7:30pm

At Cowtown Coliseum, built 1908 and host of the world’s first indoor rodeo in 1918. Tickets and schedule. Walking distance if the group stays in the Stockyards, which is most of its appeal with no cars. Ticketed

Billy Bob’s TexasLive bull riding Fri & Sat, 8:30 and 9:30pm

The world’s largest honky tonk, and a two-minute walk from Hotel Drover. The music lineup for that weekend has not been announced — that room books late. billybobstexas.com

The RusticDallas · 4.4 from 6,369 reviews

A large indoor-outdoor bar and restaurant built around a live music stage, and one of the more reliably good nights out in the Metroplex — Texas beer, a big patio, and a band most evenings. It is in Dallas rather than Fort Worth, so about 40 minutes east, which makes it a deliberate outing rather than a drop-in. Open Saturday until 1am and Sunday until 10pm. View map

Fort Worth Herd cattle driveDaily, 11:30am and 4:00pm

Longhorns driven down Exchange Avenue twice a day, every day — the world’s only twice-daily cattle drive. Takes about ten minutes and costs nothing. Details Free

Hot Wheels Monster Trucks LiveDickies Arena · four shows

Friday 7:00pm, Saturday 11:30am and 6:30pm, Sunday 1:30pm. Worth knowing chiefly because Dickies Arena sits in the same mile as the TCU stadium and the museums — four shows across three days means traffic pressure there all weekend. dickiesarena.com Ticketed

Bass Performance HallDowntown · walkable from three hotels

The Fort Worth Symphony performs Oz with Orchestra on the 13th and 14th, and When Instruments Roamed the Earth on the 14th. The venue publishes dates but not times — those sit with the symphony and need checking closer to the date. Ticketed

Dallas StarsAmerican Airlines Center · about 40 min east

Saturday the 14th against Buffalo at 7:00pm, Sunday the 15th against Florida at 7:00pm. Saturday is a real option if TCU draws an early kickoff. Ticketed

Japanese Garden & Water GardensFree or near-free

Mid-November is peak season for the maples at the Japanese Garden. The Water Gardens — Philip Johnson, 1974 — are downtown and free, so walkable from three of the hotels. fwbg.org

Section Five

Off the wall

The things that are only possible here, plus the ones that got checked and ruled out.

Worth knowing before ordering a drink

The frozen margarita was invented twenty minutes from the stadium

On 11 May 1971, a Dallas restaurateur named Mariano Martinez got tired of his bartenders failing to keep up with demand for margaritas made to his father’s recipe. He had seen a Slurpee machine in a 7-Eleven, bought a soft-serve ice cream machine, modified it, pulled the lever, and produced the world’s first frozen margarita. He never patented it. Every frozen margarita machine on earth descends from that one.

The original is now in the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, which lists it among the museum’s notable inventions. This is why Dallas calls itself the official home of the frozen margarita — a real claim, not a marketing one. Mariano’s Hacienda Ranch in Arlington, two miles from the stadium and open from 9am Sunday, carries the name.

Margaritas & More
Cowtown Tour Company · Fort Worth

A four-and-a-half hour guided tour with transportation included: Tex-Mex tasting at each stop plus a margarita per adult, meeting at the Trinity Metro Park & Ride. Nobody drives, which for a group with no cars is most of the appeal. Standard bookings run below eleven people, so eight fits comfortably.

The same operator also advertises group transport to the stadium in Arlington — which given the Sunday rideshare problem may be more useful than the tour itself.

cowtowntourco.com
ICE! at the Gaylord Texan
Grapevine · opens Friday 13 November

Two million pounds of hand-carved ice held at 9°F, with parkas provided. Ten themed rooms and six two-storey ice slides, carved by sculptors who travel in from Harbin. The 2026 theme is Harry Potter — Hogsmeade Station, the Forbidden Forest, the Great Hall — and it runs 13 November to 3 January, so opening night is the Friday the first two arrive. Tickets from around $33. Full details

It sits in the Grapevine corridor near DFW, so it pairs directly with the Hotel Vin option, or works as a Monday-morning stop on the way to a flight.

Checked, and ruled out
Three things that looked promising

NASCAR Racing Experience at Texas Motor Speedway lets you drive or ride in a real Cup car. The published 2026 dates run March through September plus one in December. There are no November dates.

The Fort Worth Margarita Festival is a May event — it ran on 16 May this year at Cullen Yards. Not that weekend.

Dallas’s Margarita Mile is real and free, but seasonal: the regular run closes around the start of November and this year’s special edition finished in July. A holiday spin-off ran from mid-November last year, so it may be live — but the dates are not published yet and it is not worth printing a trail that may be shut. Worth one recheck nearer the date.

Section Six

The museums

Worth planning around: the three major museums all close on Mondays, so the checkout day is not an option for any of them. Saturday morning before the game is the realistic window.

Kimbell Art MuseumLouis Kahn building

Photography’s First Century, from the Bibliothèque nationale de France, runs 4 October to 17 January — the first photography exhibition in the Kimbell’s history. The building alone justifies the visit. kimbellart.org Closed Mon

Amon Carter MuseumAlways free

The Statue of Liberty: from Bartholdi to Warhol, 16 August to 3 January — which pairs neatly with the fact at the top of this document. Free admission, always. cartermuseum.org Free Closed Mon

The ModernTadao Ando building

November programming has not been announced yet. The Ando building and its reflecting pond are the draw regardless. themodern.org Closed Mon

Sid Richardson MuseumSundance Square

Remington and Russell, free, downtown — walkable from three of the hotels, and the one museum that is open on Mondays, which makes it the only option before a Monday flight. sidrichardsonmuseum.org Free Open Mon

The Kimbell, the Amon Carter and the Modern sit within a few minutes’ walk of each other in the Cultural District — and of Bowie House and The Crescent. From downtown they are a short ride; from Grapevine or Arlington they are a deliberate trip.
